Jaigīṣavya
------------------------------------------
Ṛṣis or sages as described in the Hindu scriptures—especially the epics and the purāṇas—were not only persons of great spiritual eminence but also of extra-ordinary psychic and supernatural powers. जैगीषव्य was one of them.
It could be that there were more than one sage of this name.
Jaigīṣavya was one of the sons-in-law of the king Himavān. He had married Ekapāṭalā, a sister of पार्वती, the spouse of शिव (vide Harivaṁśa 1-18).
Another जैगीषव्य has been mentioned by the Devībhāgavata (9.4) as a great sage devoted to the Divine मोथेर्.
However, a more detailed account of Jaigīśavya appears in the Mahābhārata (Sabhāparva 11; Anuśāsanaparva 49; Śalyaparva 51; Śāntiparva 236). According to these descriptions, he was a man of great yogic powers, ever devoted to God and knew the secrets and intricacies of धर्म in all its aspects. He appeared as the trimūrtis (Brahmā, विष्णु and शिव) to the king Aśvaśira, exhibited his yogic powers to another sage देवल and taught the secrets of धर्म to Asita.
